memory_candidates: Lean's linter.style.longFile baseline must EQUAL the file's own round-up, not a forward-looking ceiling: setting 3400 on a 2968-line file emits 'current limit is 3400, but it is expected to be 3100' and introduces a warning. The round-up is not strictly per-hundred either -- at 3200 lines against a 3200 limit the linter demanded 3400, not 3300.

A deliberately-unread pinned binder in Lean needs TWO independent suppressions in this repo: a scoped 'set_option linter.unusedVariables false in' for the source-level linter AND an in-source @[nolint unusedArguments] attribute paired with an entry in scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt for the ENVIRONMENT linter that check-module-invariants.sh C16 reports. The environment linter is invisible to both the scoped build and the module build.
push_neg is deprecated on this toolchain (Lean v4.33.0-rc1) and emits a two-paragraph warning per use; the repository's live convention is 'push Not'.

In this repo any phase whose edits move a .lean line count will be blocked at commit by the pre-commit typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 gate; the sanctioned remedy is 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix' plus staging typst/generated/status.typ, never --no-verify. Per-phase 'Files to modify' lists should be read as implying that file.

git-commit-scoped.sh has no --allow-out-of-scope flag (that flag belongs to git-snapshot.sh); its V10 containment guard is --task-opt-in, so a required file outside state.json's declared file_scope must be landed in a separate commit invoked WITHOUT --task rather than by mutating file_scope from an implementation dispatch.
